messages:
Maria P: Quick sync — enterprise customer asked for per-tenant evidence search SLA + flexible retention profiles. They want 24h search for recent data, 7d for warm, and on-demand archive retrieval up to 90d. Can we scope a roadmap item?
Raj K: High level: two approaches — real-time indexing (expensive) vs cold-archive with query workers (cheaper but slower).
Sophie L: +1. Cost difference can be 5–10x depending on index density. We need clear SLA tiers to sell this.
Elliot Z: Proposal: define three SLA tiers: "fast" (24h indexed, realtime queries), "balanced" (7d warm index + partial results), "archival" (batch retrieval 24–72h).
Jordan Ops: Ops constraints: indexing every tenant at "fast" level needs autoscaled ingest+index nodes and ~X TB/day storage. We'd need a dedicated rollout for top customers.
Maria P: For roadmap/prioritization: suggest pilot with 2 pilot customers on "balanced" tier, evaluate cost per query and tail latency. If pilot looks good, promote to GA for paid add-on.
Raj K: Can we get rough numbers? i.e., cost per 1M events/day for each tier. Ops, can you ballpark infra?
Jordan Ops: Rough thumb: fast ~ $1200/day per TB hot index + query cluster; balanced ~ $250/day per TB (less retention index); archival ~ $30/day (cold blob + retrieval jobs). Estimates vary with compression.
Sophie L: We should include a chargeback model in pricing: allocate index cost to tenant based on retention profile and query QPS. Also add minimum commit tier for "fast".
Elliot Z: Accept criteria for launch: 1) latency SLOs for each tier documented, 2) cost model validated with pilot, 3) runbook for retrieval backfills, 4) automated per-tenant billing tags.
Maria P: Legal & compliance check: does SOC2/ISO require immediate full-text indexing for evidence retrieval?
legal-bot: For SOC2/ISO evidence, requirement is demonstrable access within contractual windows; not necessarily realtime indexing. Need ability to produce unaltered evidence and chain-of-custody. Document retrieval SLA must be met per contract.
Sophie L: That means archival approach is acceptable as long as chain-of-custody and integrity checks exist. We still need to surface a clear customer-facing SLA table.
Raj K: Technical note: we can implement hybrid: prefix-KV caching for recent requests + background indexer for warm data. That reduces p99 for common queries.
Jordan Ops: Implementation risks: search index rebuilds after schema changes, cross-region replication for compliance, and tenant isolation for BYOK customers. Expect 2–3 sprints for PoC infra.
Maria P: BYOK/KMS customers are special case — keys might prevent us from indexing plaintext. We need guidance: either index derived metadata (hashes, tokens) or run indexing within customer's VPC/private deployment.
Elliot Z: Recommendation: for BYOK, offer only "balanced" and "archival" unless customer opts for private deployment. Add note in roadmap docs.
Sophie L: UX ask: admin UI to set retention profile per tenant, with cost preview and warnings for compliance-sensitive tenants.
Raj K: Can we add a minimal prototype: a CLI and API to set profile, plus telemetry export? That helps sales demos.
Maria P: Action items: (1) Jordan + Elliot to draft infra PoC plan and cost model (due EOD Tue), (2) Sophie to mock pricing tiers and admin UI flows, (3) Legal to prepare contract language for retrieval SLA and BYOK constraints.
legal-bot: I'll prepare templated SLA wording and BYOK caveats.
Jordan Ops: I'll also spike cross-region replication and rough infra cost by Friday.
Elliot Z: I'll outline acceptance tests and a prompt set for quality checks for evidence retrieval.
Maria P: Thanks — we'll review in roadmap sync Thurs. :thumbsup:
Sophie L: +1, will add to the product board and tag pilot customers.
Raj K: Closing note — want to ensure we capture telemetry events for billing + audit. Make sure it ties to token-level cost in Redwood Console.
Maria P: Agreed. End thread.
